label: REQUIRES_LACK_2: what a determination is, as realized in a bearer, makes it lack members of a set
term: requires the lack of, in a bearer (RequiresLackIn ReqIn x d S)
definition: RequiresLackIn ReqIn x d S: it belongs to what the determination d is, as realized in the bearer x, that x does not have every member of the set S. It is bearer-relative: d's requiring a lack in x says nothing about other bearers of d. Examples: in a simple being whose one nature excludes k, each determination of that being, as realized in it (being, on the identity thesis for simple beings, that one nature), requires the lack of k in it; a human's finite intellect, as realized in that human, requires the lack of knowing infinitely many truths at once. Non-example: a requirement of the same determination in a different bearer. Distinguishing conditions: REQUIRES_LACK_1 (RequiresLack d S, DEF 88f7c656) is type-level and binds every bearer of d, and it is the sense in which member grounding (89c988d9) and the purity of requirements (0c8631bd) are stated; REQUIRES_LACK_2 does not bind the bearer-neutral admissible family through member grounding. Every requirement as such of a determination x has is plausibly a requirement in x (the converse bridge, not asserted); the passage from in-x to as-such is the open bridge RootRequirementsInHoldAsSuch, false for a determination shared with a bearer that has the excluded items. Structural properties: none encoded; it is a declared primitive ReqIn : B → D → Set D → Prop.
note: Stipulative analyst notion for #2145 lane U, attribution deferred. Introduced because the unity argument's natural transfer (the one constituent of a simple being is, in reality, each determination it realizes) reaches requirements in the bearer, not requirements as such. See docs/notes/causal-perfection-transfer.md, section 'Carriage from the unity of a simple root'.
